summary: No vulnerabilities found. Hidden-information boundary (REQ-025/REQ-043.6) holds. Data path traced: TableState.hand -> completedHand (src/table/session.ts:721-746) copies only userHoleCards for the user plus shown = showdownOf(hand) (src/engine/player-view.ts:124-132), which maps result.showdown; HandResult.showdown is populated by revealShown (src/engine/hand.ts:526-552) with shown seats only, mucked seats excluded, and is [] / null for a fold-out. shownOpponents (src/table/review.ts:200-213) reads only hand.shown, hand.seats (names), hand.userSeat and hand.board; it never touches hand.players, hand.deck or the replay code (review.ts imports ReplayCode as a type only). Table.tsx reviewHeader spreads exactly {summary, shown} into ReviewPanel, and ReviewPanel is the only consumer. In the panel, each ShownOpponent renders as React text, an aria-label attribute and PlayingCard data-card/aria-label for the two shown cards; there is no dangerouslySetInnerHTML. Seat names come from validated session config (1-40 chars) and React escapes them. The user's own seat is filtered out, so nothing new about the user leaks. No new dependencies, randomness, storage, logging or secrets. Tests: SPEC-05 does a static source ban on shuffledDeck/createHand/dealHand in the three review sources, and the acceptance and e2e tests search the rendered panel for every folded and mucked card. This is adequate for the change.
